record.original_question: If K(X) has property U in the linear span of K(X) together with the identity operator I_X, must K(X) also have property U in the whole operator space L(X)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a Banach space. Denote by $L(X)$ the Banach space of all bounded linear operators on $X$ (with the operator norm), by $K(X)$ its closed subspace of compact operators, and by $I_X$ the identity operator on $X$. Let $E := \mathrm{span}(K(X) \cup \{I_X\}) \subseteq L(X)$.

Recall that a closed subspace $Y$ of a Banach space $Z$ is said to have property $U$ in $Z$ (in the sense of Phelps) if every continuous linear functional $y^* \in Y^*$ admits a unique norm-preserving extension to a continuous linear functional on $Z$.

Question: Suppose $K(X)$ has property $U$ in $E = \mathrm{span}(K(X) \cup \{I_X\})$. Must $K(X)$ then have property $U$ in $L(X)$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search returned general references on Phelps' property U and on relations between property U of K(X) in L(X) and geometric properties of X, but no source resolving the specific lifting question from span(K(X) ∪ {I_X}) to all of L(X). The analogous statement for M-ideals is known to be true, but no published resolution of the property-U version was located, so the status is treated as unknown.

status_evidence.title: On subspaces of Banach spaces where every functional has a unique norm-preserving extension
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Phelps' property U and gives geometric characterizations; discusses property U for K(E,F) in L(E,F).
status_evidence.claim: Property U for compact-operator subspaces is an active topic but the specific lifting question is not addressed conclusively.

status_evidence.title: Linear Hahn–Banach extension operators
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses uniqueness of Hahn–Banach extensions in operator spaces.
status_evidence.claim: General context on Hahn–Banach uniqueness; no resolution of the specific problem.
